Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing: traffic profile & SLA budget

Hi Claire / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our discussion, to produce a concrete Dedicated sizing recommendation and a baseline fleet outline we need a concise traffic profile from your side. I’ve attached a short questionnaire but a quick CSV will also work. Specifically we need:

- Typical and peak QPS (1min/5min peaks) for real-time endpoints
- Percentage split realtime vs batch (async) workloads
- Concurrency per user/session and expected global concurrency
- Average prompt tokens and average response tokens; p95/p99 lengths if you have them
- Distribution of model variants (e.g., base Llama2-70B, quantized 4-bit, or specific SFTs)
- Traffic cadence (regular daily peaks, weekend spikes, quarterly events) and expected burst durations
- Warm-up behavior (cold starts frequency, need for pre-warmed KV caches)
- SLOs (p95 / p99 latency targets) and cost constraints we should optimize for

If you prefer, fill the attached PDF or paste the answers inline — either way we can turn this into a mutual action plan and an initial hardware map (GPU types, count, and reserve buffer).

Deliverable: initial fleet outline + cost range by EOD Friday once we have the profile.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing: traffic profile & SLA budget

Tessa — attaching the CSV export from our edge gateway that captures last 30 days. Below are the highlights, let me know if you want raw logs instead.

Key metrics (last 30d):
- Typical steady-state QPS: 28
- 95th percentile 1-min peak QPS: 220 (15:30 PST daily)
- 5-min sustained peaks: 150
- Batch jobs (nightly re-rank & embeddings): 30 concurrent workers during 02:00–04:00 PST
- Realtime vs batch: ~85% realtime, 15% batch
- Global concurrency: active sessions ~1,800, typical concurrent requests ~350; expected growth ~30% q/q
- Avg prompt tokens: 80 tokens; avg response tokens: 420 tokens
- p95 response tokens: 1,400 tokens; p99: 2,200 tokens (long re-rank chains)
- Models in use: finetuned-llama2-13B (60%), off-the-shelf-70B-quant (30%), experimental-7B (10%)
- Target SLO: p95 latency <= 350ms for realtime text-gen (we can relax to 1.5s for long-form re-rank)
- Burst characteristics: short spikes (30–90s) at market open + promotional events causing sustained 10–15min increases
- Cold starts: ~5% of requests hit cold replicas after weekends; pre-warm would help for the 70B quant variant

Attaching: aurora_traffic_profile_dec0726.csv (sample broken into 1m bins).

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through specifics.

Thanks,
Claire Huang
Head of ML Platforms | Aurora Retail

Forwarding Claire’s profile and a couple quick clarification asks so we can size the GPU mix: see questions inline.

On Tue, Dec 7, 2026 at 10:03 AM Claire Huang <claire@aurora-retail.com> wrote:
> (CSV attached)
> ...summary...

Dev’s clarifications:
1) For the p95/p99 token lengths you gave, are those per-request total tokens (prompt + response) or response tokens only?
2) Of the 30% traffic on the 70B-quant variant, what's the expected tolerance to <100ms p95 latency degradation if we route to a 13B quantized fallback during extreme burst? (helps us propose a cost-saving fallback policy)
3) Do batch jobs tolerate preemption/spot-style capacity? If yes, we can offload to spot pools and shrink dedicated baseline.
4) Can you share a sample of the largest re-rank chains (we only need a 1–2 examples) so we can estimate KV-cache and attention working set sizes for 70B runs?

If Claire can answer these, we can produce: baseline fleet (GPU type + counts), recommended warm pool size, and an SLA-backed canary plan.

—Dev
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Claire Huang <claire@aurora-retail.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing: traffic profile & SLA budget

Thanks Dev — answers inline:
1) p95/p99 token lengths are response tokens only (we truncate prompts where possible). Total end-to-end tokens typically add ~120 tokens for context.
2) For the 70B-quant variant, the team can tolerate up to ~200ms p95 degradation for non-critical endpoints (re-rank). For core customer-facing conversational flows we want <350ms p95 — routing to 13B is acceptable during sustained >1k QPS events but not for short 30–90s microbursts.
3) Batch jobs are flexible — they can run on preemptible/spot capacity; only nightly re-rank windows need to be completed by 06:00 PST.
4) Attaching two anonymized re-rank traces (included in CSV rows 12–13). They show chains of 4–7 model calls with intermediate context caching.

Let us know if you want a 30–45m walkthrough tomorrow.

—Claire
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@aurora-retail.com>, Samir Patel <samir.ops@aurora-retail.com>

Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing: traffic profile & SLA budget — initial fleet outline + next steps

Claire / Samir — thanks for the swift follow-ups and the traces. Based on the CSV and clarifications, we propose the attached initial fleet outline (summary below). This is a conservative baseline to meet your p95 SLAs with room for 30% growth; we can tighten after a 2-week pilot.

Baseline recommendation (production):
- 8 x H100-80GB (latency-sensitive fleet) running mixed precision for 13B finetuned model; reserved warm pool = 2 GPUs for KV cache priming
- 6 x A100-80GB (cost-optimized fleet) for the 70B-quant variant with quantization-aware paths; warm pool = 1 GPU (pre-warmed quin)
- Batch/async: spot pool of up to 10 x A10 / equivalently priced GPUs for nightly re-rank and embeddings jobs (preemptible OK)
- Autoscale policy: scale by sustained 1-min QPS > 120 for more than 3 mins; burst headroom: keep 20% spare capacity for 1–2min microbursts, for longer bursts use fast fallback routing to 13B
- Routing policy: latenciesensitive endpoints pinned to H100 pool; re-rank flows to A100 with fallback to 13B when tail latency risk detected
- Expected delivered p95: ~260–320ms (meets target <=350ms); p99 will be higher for 70B chains — we recommend an SLA exception for p99 on long re-rank jobs or route them as batch.

Estimated monthly cost band (in USD, incl. reserved capacity + ops): $145k–$190k (range depends on utilization and spot success for batch). Detailed cost model in the attached PDF.

Next steps:
1) Sign off on the baseline fleet so we can provision a pilot environment (2–4 week pilot).
2) Schedule a 45m pilot kickoff to confirm warm pool sizing and run a 48h load replay (we’ll use your CSV).
3) Post-pilot: finalize SLA language for p95/p99 and optional dedicated burst buffer (additional reserved GPUs).

Attachments: initial_fleet_outline_AUR-2026-1092.pdf (3 pages)

If that looks good I’ll drop a short mutual action plan into HubSpot and loop Legal for the usual Dedicated onboarding docs.

Best,
